solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: 'hagiography' is a low-frequency word; many test-takers will pick by elimination, and 'polemic' (an attack, the opposite of what's needed) may draw students who only sense 'a book with a strong slant'
S008-01.notes: Critics expected a flattering account because the author was a 20-year aide; 'Instead... unsparing' sets up the contrast. Hagiography means an idealizing biography. Polemic and satire are hostile, which is what the book actually is. Chronicle is neutral and gives no contrast.

S008-02.notes: Sentence 2 says nighttime temperatures matter for health (the body recovers only at night), which explains why Asante's nighttime measurements matter. A is wrong because the measurements support it. C is wrong because no methods are given. D is wrong because sentence 2 is not about daytime studies.

flags: minor: C is the longest and most detailed choice, which is a length tell
S008-03.notes: The text gives the overfishing explanation, shows evidence against it (limits tightened, decline continued), offers the dams explanation, and reports support for it (counts tripled after the dams came out). A fits loosely, but the solution did not fail. B: only one river. D: the hypothesis was tested.

flags: minor: D is the longest choice and the only one that states the gap explicitly, which is a test-wise tell
minor: D's wording 'Species A fell from 70% to 63%' leaves out the word 'success', but it is still clear
S008-04.notes: The claim is about the gap narrowing. Only D uses both endpoints for both species: 30 points to 3 points (70-40 and 63-60 both check out). B covers only one species. C gives a single year. A is irrelevant.

S008-05.notes: Weeds let caterpillars grow large before they reach the cotton, and large caterpillars resist the toxin, so removing the weeds should improve effectiveness. B: no evidence the toxin breaks down. C: unsupported. D: 'at every stage' overstates the passage, since they do move to cotton.

S008-06.notes: The appositive noun phrase 'a phrase that later became...' must be set off by a comma, placed inside the closing quotation mark. A has no punctuation. B uses a semicolon before a non-independent clause. D adds commas inside the quoted phrase, which breaks it up.

S008-07.notes: The opening participial phrase ('Having spent three years collecting...') must modify Ruiz, so the subject has to be Ruiz. A, B and C make the committee, Ruiz's methods, or praise the subject, which leaves the modifier dangling. In D, 'she' then refers back correctly.

S008-08.notes: No harm to overall ridership, yet the committee recommends restoring routes anyway, which is a concessive contrast, so 'Still'. 'Thus' implies the recommendation follows from the finding. 'For example' and 'Likewise' do not fit.

flags: minor: A is the only choice that both defines the device and states its value, so the answer stands out at a glance
S008-09.notes: The goal is to explain to an unfamiliar audience why long records are valuable. A defines a tide gauge and says long records track average sea level. B and C give details without the value. D is not drawn from the notes and is vague.

S008-10.notes: Base-rate reasoning: drinking the brand is no more common among people with the condition (80%) than in the general population (about 80%), so the survey gives little evidence of causation. A overreaches in the other direction. B contradicts the data. C is unsupported.
